description: Small self-contained RAG retrieval evaluation set. A retrieved chunk counts as relevant when its text contains one of the sample's relevant_phrases (case-insensitive) or its id is listed in relevant_chunk_ids. Phrase matching keeps the dataset independent of the random chunk ids created at indexing time.

documents.name: ml_basics
pages: Machine learning is a field of artificial intelligence in which computers learn patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules. A trained model can then make predictions about new, unseen examples.
Supervised learning trains a model on labeled examples, where every input comes with the correct output. Typical supervised tasks are classification of emails as spam and regression of house prices.
Unsupervised learning works with unlabeled data and tries to discover hidden structure. Clustering with k-means groups similar customers together without any predefined categories.
Overfitting happens when a model memorizes the training data and performs poorly on new data. Regularization and cross-validation are common ways to reduce overfitting.
Neural networks consist of layers of connected neurons that transform their inputs with weights and activation functions. Backpropagation adjusts the weights by computing gradients of the loss.

documents.name: databases_basics
pages: A relational database stores data in tables made of rows and columns. SQL is the standard language used to query and modify relational data.
A primary key uniquely identifies each row in a table, while a foreign key links a row to a row in another table and enforces referential integrity.
Database normalization organizes tables to reduce redundancy. The third normal form removes columns that depend on non-key attributes.
An index is a data structure such as a B-tree that speeds up lookups on a column at the cost of extra storage and slower writes.
A transaction groups several operations into one unit of work. ACID properties guarantee atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.
